question: In case of jelly, which of the following is the dispersed phase?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Liquid phase**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In jelly, the dispersed phase is the **liquid phase** while the dispersion medium is the solid phase.
 
• Jelly is a type of **gel** where the liquid phase is dispersed in the solid network.
 
• The liquid phase in jelly provides the fluidity and moisture content of the gel.
 
• During the jelly-making process, the liquid phase solidifies upon cooling, forming a semi-solid structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dispersed Phase:**

 
 
• The dispersed phase refers to the phase that is distributed or spread throughout another continuous phase known as the dispersion medium.
 
• In the context of colloids, the dispersed phase can be solid, liquid, or gas.
 
 
 
• **Dispersion Medium:**
 
 
• The dispersion medium is the continuous phase in which the dispersed phase is distributed.
 
• The dispersion medium can also be solid, liquid, or gas.
 
 
 
• **Colloids:**
 
 
• Colloids are mixtures where one substance is dispersed evenly throughout another without dissolving.
 
• Common types of colloids include gels, sols, emulsions, and foams.
 
 
 
• **Gel:**
 
 
• A gel is a colloidal system in which the dispersed phase is a liquid and the dispersion medium is a solid.
 
• Gels exhibit a semi-solid state and have properties of both solids and liquids.
